```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 4.0, dpi = 300, dev = "png")
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

repo_root <- if (file.exists("Second Step/results/results_all.csv")) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists("../Second Step/results/results_all.csv")) {
  ".."
} else {
  stop("Cannot locate Second Step/results/results_all.csv")
}

fmt <- function(x, d = 4) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)

between_arm_ss <- function(values, arms) {
  arms <- droplevels(as.factor(arms))
  overall_mean <- mean(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  arm_means <- tapply(values, arms, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  arm_counts <- table(arms)
  sum(arm_counts[names(arm_means)] * (arm_means - overall_mean)^2)
}

conditions <- read.delim(
  file.path(repo_root, "conditions.tsv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  na.strings = ""
)

# --- Composer-2 run (Second Step) ---
results_c2 <- read.csv(
  file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/results/results_all.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    arm = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", agent_id),
    arm = factor(arm, levels = conditions$condition),
    years_start = as.integer(years_start),
    years_end = as.integer(years_end),
    year_span = years_end - years_start + 1,
    cov_none = grepl("^none$|^$", tolower(trimws(covariates))),
    est_lc = tolower(trimws(estimator)),
    twfe = grepl("twfe|feols|fixest", est_lc),
    continuous_tx = grepl("continuous", tolower(treatment_definition)),
    model = "composer-2"
  )

arm_summary_c2 <- results_c2 |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_att = mean(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_att = sd(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_att = median(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_negative = mean(att_estimate < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_teen = mean(outcome_variable == "emp_pop_ratio_teen", na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_no_cov = mean(cov_none, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_twfe = mean(twfe, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_continuous = mean(continuous_tx, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_start = mean(years_start, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_span = mean(year_span, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

set.seed(42)
obs_stat_c2 <- between_arm_ss(results_c2$att_estimate, results_c2$arm)
perm_stats_c2 <- replicate(10000, {
  between_arm_ss(results_c2$att_estimate, sample(results_c2$arm))
})
fisher_p_c2 <- mean(perm_stats_c2 >= obs_stat_c2)
kw_c2 <- kruskal.test(att_estimate ~ arm, data = results_c2)
```

## Executive summary

This project tests whether **prompted literature priors** causally change what autonomous AI agents report about the employment effects of the minimum wage. Agents analyze the **same** state–year panel with the **same** task instructions; only the literature context (if any) is randomized. Multiple AI models are tested to examine whether model choice mediates the influence of literature primes.

**Design.** Five arms × 50 Cursor agents per model. Arms: no prime; null-effect short; null-effect with citations; negative-effect short; negative-effect with citations. Agents choose outcome, sample window, treatment definition, covariates, and estimator under a shared DiD methodology guide.

**Headline results — Composer-2 run (Second Step, 250 agents).**

| Finding | Result |
|:--------|:-------|
| Completion | **250/250** agents returned usable `results.csv` |
| Between-arm ATT differences | **Not significant** (Fisher omnibus *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p_c2)`; Kruskal–Wallis *p* = `r fmt(kw_c2$p.value)`) |
| Outcome choice | **~99.6%** studied teen employment-to-population |
| Estimator choice | **~98.8%** Callaway–Sant'Anna family; **≤4% TWFE** in any arm |
| Treatment definition | **249/250 binary**; **0% continuous** MW treatment |
| Short vs citation-rich primes | **No meaningful ATT gap** on planned contrasts |

**Headline results — Opus 4.6 run (Third Step, 249 agents, 1 failure).**

| Finding | Result |
|:--------|:-------|
| Completion | **249/250** agents returned usable `results.csv` |
| Between-arm ATT differences | **Significant** (Fisher omnibus *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p_opus)`; Kruskal–Wallis *p* = `r fmt(kw_opus$p.value)`) |
| Outlier arm | **`negative_short`**: mean ATT = `r fmt(arm_summary_opus$mean_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"])`, median = `r fmt(arm_summary_opus$median_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"])` (most negative) |
| Specification variation | `negative_short` shows **3 continuous treatment**, **2 CGBS**, **1 TWFE** — more diverse than other arms |
| Pairwise | `null_cites` vs `negative_short` *p* = `r fmt(pw_opus$p.value["null_cites", "negative_short"])` |

**Headline results — Grok 4.6 v1 (with CS recipe, 245 agents).**

| Finding | Result |
|:--------|:-------|
| Between-arm ATT differences | **Highly significant** (Fisher *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p_grok)`; KW *p* = `r sprintf("%.1e", kw_grok$p.value)`) |
| Planned contrasts | Null Short − Neg Short *p* < 0.0001; Null Cites − Neg Cites *p* = 0.0004 |
| Mechanism | **Both** negative arms shift left via **outcome variable + control group** choice (100% CS, 100% binary) |

**Headline results — Grok 4.6 v2 (neutralized instructions, 243 agents).**

| Finding | Result |
|:--------|:-------|
| Between-arm ATT differences | **Highly significant** (Fisher *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p_grok2)`; KW *p* = `r sprintf("%.1e", kw_grok2$p.value)`) |
| Estimator adoption | **100% Callaway–Sant'Anna** despite removing CS recipe |
| Implication | CS preference is from model training, **not** the instruction document |

**Bottom line.** Literature primes produce **model-dependent** effects through **different specification channels**:

- **Composer-2:** No detectable prime effect (Wave 1-like).
- **Opus 4.6:** `negative_short` arm diverges via estimator/treatment switching (Wave 2-like).
- **Grok 4.6:** Both negative arms diverge via outcome variable and control group selection — **the strongest prime effect observed**, and the mechanism persists identically when the CS step-by-step recipe is removed.

**Implication.** The mechanism through which priors affect estimates varies by model. Removing instructional scaffolding does not eliminate the prime effect — agents' specification choices are shaped by model training, not the methodology document.

---

## 1. Purpose and motivation

Many-analyst studies show that researchers facing identical data can report different causal estimates through **specification choices**. Borjas & Breznau (2026, *Science Advances*) linked immigration researchers' priors to their estimates. Scott Cunningham's design turns that association into an **experiment** by randomizing the prior via a literature prime while holding data and task fixed ([Substack write-up](https://causalinf.substack.com/p/claude-code-45-ai-agents-and-the)).

This repository is a **Cursor SDK replication / extension** of Cunningham's `mw-analyst-experiment` design (originally Claude Code CLI).

**Research question:** Do literature primes about minimum-wage employment effects causally shift autonomous agents' reported average treatment effects (ATTs)?

---

## 2. Experimental design

### Arms

| Arm ID | Label | Literature file |
|:-------|:------|:----------------|
| `none` | None | *(none)* |
| `null_short` | Null Short | `PRIME_NULL_SHORT.md` |
| `null_cites` | Null Cites | `PRIME_NULL_CITES.md` |
| `negative_short` | Negative Short | `PRIME_NEGATIVE_SHORT.md` |
| `negative_cites` | Negative Cites | `PRIME_NEGATIVE_CITES.md` |

All agents receive: `agent_panel_essential.csv`, `DATA_DICTIONARY.md`, `DID_METHODOLOGY.md`, and `INSTRUCTIONS_SHARED.md`. Primed arms also receive one literature context file.

### What agents decide

- Employment outcome (CPS subgroups, QCEW industries, etc.)
- Treatment definition (binary staggered vs continuous)
- Sample years / states
- Covariates and comparison group
- Estimator (Callaway–Sant'Anna, continuous DiD, TWFE, etc.)

### Deliverables per agent

1. **`results.csv`** — one row with design choices and ATT / SE / CI  
2. **`llms.txt`** — structured narrative of the analysis  

### Data

Pre-aggregated **state × year** panel (51 units, 1990–2022): effective minimum wages, CPS employment rates for multiple groups, and selected QCEW industry series.

### Scale and waves

| Wave | Location | Scale | Model | Notes |
|:-----|:---------|:------|:------|:------|
| First | `First Step/` | 150 agents (30×5) | `composer-2` | Earlier protocol; TWFE discouraged |
| Second | `Second Step/results/` | **250 agents (50×5)** | `composer-2` | TWFE allowed in methodology |
| Third | `Third Step/results_opus46/` | **249 agents (50×5, 1 failure)** | **`opus-4.6`** | Same protocol as Second |
| Fourth | `Third Step/results_grok46/` | **245 agents (50×5, 5 failures)** | **`grok-4.6`** | Same protocol as Second |
| Fifth | `Third Step/results_grok46_v2/` | **243 agents (50×5, 7 failures)** | **`grok-4.6`** | **Neutralized instructions**: CS recipe + recommendations removed |

---

## 3. Technical pipeline

| Component | Role |
|:----------|:-----|
| `@cursor/sdk` + `launch_experiment_cursor.mjs` | Local agents in isolated temp workspaces |
| `run_full_experiment.sh` / `run_pilot_one_per_condition.sh` | Full (250) and pilot (5) launchers |
| `collect_results.sh` | Aggregate outputs → `Second Step/results/` |
| `analyze_results.R` | Omnibus tests, plots |
| `analyze_second_step_detail.R` | Extended tables/figures → `Second Step/analysis/` |

Models: **`composer-2`** (Second Step), **`opus-4.6`** (Third Step), **`grok-4.6`** (Third Step, two runs: v1 with full instructions, v2 with neutralized instructions). Agents are sandboxed with `settingSources: []` so user/project rules outside the workspace are not loaded.

---

## 4. Key results — Composer-2 run (Second Step, *N* = 250)

### Arm-level ATT summary

```{r arm-table-c2}
arm_summary_c2 |>
  transmute(
    Arm = as.character(arm),
    N = n,
    `Mean ATT` = fmt(mean_att),
    `SD` = fmt(sd_att),
    `Median` = fmt(median_att),
    `% neg.` = fmt(100 * frac_negative, 1),
    `% teen` = fmt(100 * frac_teen, 1),
    `% TWFE` = fmt(100 * frac_twfe, 1),
    `Mean span` = fmt(mean_span, 1)
  ) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
        caption = "Composer-2 arm-level ATT summary (Second Step).")
```

### Inference

- **Fisher omnibus** (between-arm sum of squares, 10,000 permutations): observed = `r fmt(obs_stat_c2)`, *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p_c2)`.
- **Kruskal–Wallis** across five arms: χ² = `r fmt(kw_c2$statistic)`, *p* = `r fmt(kw_c2$p.value)`.
- Planned contrasts (null − negative, short and cites): neither rejects at conventional levels.

**Interpretation:** condition labels are statistically exchangeable with respect to reported ATT in the composer-2 run.

```{r fig-att-c2, fig.cap="Distribution of reported ATT estimates by treatment arm — Composer-2 (N = 250)."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/results/att_by_arm.png"))
```

```{r fig-forest-c2, fig.cap="Arm-level mean ATT with approximate 95% intervals — Composer-2."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/analysis/forest_arm_means.png"))
```

### Specification patterns (Composer-2)

- **Outcome:** nearly universal teen EMP/POP (`emp_pop_ratio_teen`).
- **Estimator:** Callaway–Sant'Anna dominates; TWFE rare and not concentrated in negative arms.
- **Treatment:** almost entirely binary staggered MW changes.
- **Covariates:** nontrivial share use none (~42–66% by arm); not clearly sorted by prime.
- **Event studies:** produced by ≥98% of agents per arm.

```{r fig-estimator-c2, fig.cap="Estimator family composition by arm — Composer-2."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/analysis/estimator_family_stacked_by_arm.png"))
```

## 5. Key results — Opus 4.6 run (Third Step, *N* = 249)

The Opus 4.6 run used the **identical protocol, data, and instructions** as the Composer-2 Second Step, differing only in the underlying AI model (`claude-opus-4-6` via Cursor SDK). One agent failed, yielding 249 usable results (49 in `negative_cites`, 50 in all other arms).

### Arm-level ATT summary

```{r arm-table-opus}
arm_summary_opus |>
  transmute(
    Arm = as.character(arm),
    N = n,
    `Mean ATT` = fmt(mean_att),
    `SD` = fmt(sd_att),
    `Median` = fmt(median_att),
    `% neg.` = fmt(100 * frac_negative, 1),
    `% teen` = fmt(100 * frac_teen, 1),
    `% TWFE` = fmt(100 * frac_twfe, 1),
    `% continuous` = fmt(100 * frac_continuous, 1),
    `Mean span` = fmt(mean_span, 1)
  ) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", rep("r", 9)),
        caption = "Opus 4.6 arm-level ATT summary (Third Step).")
```

### Inference

```{r inference-opus}
cat(sprintf("- **Fisher omnibus** (between-arm SS, 10,000 permutations): observed = %s, *p* = %s\n",
            fmt(obs_stat_opus), fmt(fisher_p_opus)))
cat(sprintf("- **Kruskal–Wallis** (all five arms): chi-squared = %s, *p* = %s\n",
            fmt(kw_opus$statistic), fmt(kw_opus$p.value)))
```

**The between-arm difference is statistically significant.** The `negative_short` arm is the clear outlier: mean ATT = `r fmt(arm_summary_opus$mean_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"])`, median = `r fmt(arm_summary_opus$median_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"])` — the most negative of all five arms.

**Pairwise comparisons** (Wilcoxon rank-sum, unadjusted):

```{r pairwise-opus}
pw_df <- as.data.frame(pw_opus$p.value)
pw_df <- tibble(
  Comparison = paste(rep(rownames(pw_opus$p.value), each = ncol(pw_opus$p.value)),
                     "vs",
                     rep(colnames(pw_opus$p.value), times = nrow(pw_opus$p.value))),
  p_value = as.vector(as.matrix(pw_opus$p.value))
) |>
  filter(!is.na(p_value)) |>
  arrange(p_value) |>
  mutate(p_value = fmt(p_value))
kable(pw_df, booktabs = TRUE, col.names = c("Comparison", "p-value"),
      caption = "Pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (Opus 4.6 run, unadjusted).")
```

```{r fig-att-opus, fig.cap="Distribution of reported ATT estimates by treatment arm — Opus 4.6 (N = 249)."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Third Step/results_opus46/att_by_arm.png"))
```

### Specification patterns (Opus 4.6)

The `negative_short` arm shows meaningfully **more specification diversity** than other arms:

- **3 agents** used **continuous treatment** definitions (vs 0 in other arms).
- **2 agents** used **CGBS / continuous DiD** estimators.
- **1 agent** used **TWFE**.
- **11 agents** used **never-treated** as the control group (vs predominantly not-yet-treated in other arms).
- The remaining agents used Callaway–Sant'Anna, consistent with the overall pattern.

This specification variation in the `negative_short` arm is reminiscent of Cunningham's **Wave 2** finding: negatively primed agents exercising more estimator discretion. A Fisher exact test of treatment definition (binary vs continuous) × arm yields *p* ≈ 0.051 (borderline).

---

## 6. Cross-model comparison

```{r cross-model-omnibus}
cross_omnibus <- tibble(
  Model = c("Composer-2", "Opus 4.6", "Grok 4.6 (v1)", "Grok 4.6 (v2, neutralized)"),
  N = c(nrow(results_c2), nrow(results_opus), nrow(results_grok), nrow(results_grok2)),
  `Fisher p` = c(fmt(fisher_p_c2), fmt(fisher_p_opus), fmt(fisher_p_grok), fmt(fisher_p_grok2)),
  `KW p` = c(fmt(kw_c2$p.value), fmt(kw_opus$p.value),
             sprintf("%.1e", kw_grok$p.value), sprintf("%.1e", kw_grok2$p.value)),
  `Primary channel` = c("—", "Estimator/treatment", "Outcome + control group", "Outcome + control group"),
  `Significant?` = c("No", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes")
)
kable(cross_omnibus, booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "l", "c"),
      caption = "Omnibus tests across all model runs.")
```

```{r cross-model-neg-short}
neg_short_compare <- tibble(
  Model = c("Composer-2", "Opus 4.6", "Grok 4.6 v1", "Grok 4.6 v2"),
  `Mean ATT (neg_short)` = c(
    fmt(arm_summary_c2$mean_att[arm_summary_c2$arm == "negative_short"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_opus$mean_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_grok$mean_att[arm_summary_grok$arm == "negative_short"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_grok2$mean_att[arm_summary_grok2$arm == "negative_short"])
  ),
  `Mean ATT (none)` = c(
    fmt(arm_summary_c2$mean_att[arm_summary_c2$arm == "none"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_opus$mean_att[arm_summary_opus$arm == "none"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_grok$mean_att[arm_summary_grok$arm == "none"]),
    fmt(arm_summary_grok2$mean_att[arm_summary_grok2$arm == "none"])
  ),
  `% CS` = c("98.8%", "94.0%", "100%", "100%"),
  `% non-teen (neg_short)` = c(
    fmt(100 * (1 - arm_summary_c2$frac_teen[arm_summary_c2$arm == "negative_short"]), 0),
    fmt(100 * (1 - arm_summary_opus$frac_teen[arm_summary_opus$arm == "negative_short"]), 0),
    fmt(100 * (1 - arm_summary_grok$frac_teen[arm_summary_grok$arm == "negative_short"]), 0),
    fmt(100 * (1 - arm_summary_grok2$frac_teen[arm_summary_grok2$arm == "negative_short"]), 0)
  )
)
kable(neg_short_compare, booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", rep("r", 4)),
      caption = "negative\\_short arm across models: ATT and specification patterns.")
```

**Key findings:**

1. **Model is a first-order moderator.** The same protocol yields no prime effect with `composer-2`, a moderate effect with `opus-4.6`, and a strong effect with `grok-4.6`.
2. **The mechanism varies by model.** Opus shifts through estimator/treatment switching; Grok shifts through outcome variable and control group selection.
3. **Removing the CS recipe has no effect on estimator choice** (Grok v1 vs v2: both 100% CS). The CS preference is baked into model training.
4. **Removing the not-yet-treated recommendation shifts control group choices** in non-primed arms but does not change the prime effect magnitude.

---

## 7. Comparison to Cunningham (2026)

| Dimension | Cunningham (Substack) | Composer-2 | Opus 4.6 | Grok 4.6 |
|:----------|:----------------------|:-----------|:---------|:---------|
| Platform | Claude Code CLI | Cursor SDK | Cursor SDK | Cursor SDK |
| Wave 1 pattern | Similar ATTs (CS-only) | **Replicates** | Partial | — |
| Wave 2 pattern | Neg arm → TWFE, more negative | **Does not replicate** | **Partially** (neg\_short) | **Novel channel** (outcome + control) |
| Mechanism | Estimator switching | — | Estimator switching | Outcome + control group |
| Prime effect strength | Moderate–strong | None | Moderate | **Strong** |

Cunningham's central finding — negatively primed agents exercise more specification discretion and report more negative ATTs — **replicates across models but through different channels**. Opus 4.6 mirrors the Wave 2 estimator-switching pattern. Grok 4.6 discovers a **novel mechanism**: outcome variable and control group selection, while staying entirely on Callaway–Sant'Anna.

The **instruction-neutralization experiment** (Grok v2) demonstrates that agents' estimator preferences come from **model training, not the methodology document**. This has implications for experimental design: the CS recipe was not driving CS adoption, so removing it does not "free" agents to explore TWFE.

## 9. Limitations and next steps

**Limitations.** Three models tested (`composer-2`, `opus-4.6`, `grok-4.6`); no rhetoric/confidence scoring pipeline; prime texts differ from Cunningham's exact wording; within-model instruction variation tested only for Grok.

**Testable next steps.**

1. Match Cunningham's three-arm primes and Wave 2 methodology text verbatim for a direct comparison.
2. Run the neutralized-instruction variant on **Opus 4.6** to test whether its estimator-switching channel also persists without the CS recipe.
3. Inspect agent logs for the `negative_short` arm across models to trace specification-search mechanisms in detail.
4. Test additional models (e.g., GPT-5.6, Fable 5.1) to map the full model → prime-sensitivity frontier.
5. Add Cunningham-style rhetoric/confidence scoring to test whether prime effects show up in narrative even when ATTs don't shift.
